transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Derek Shaw (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Redwood CSM); Priya Menon (Head of ML Ops), Markus Voss (CTO), Jolie Kim (SRE), Evan Reed (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Obsidian is evaluating a 20-35% capacity uplift and adding EU and APAC regions; they are still considering private deployment pilot for sensitive PII workloads. Key blockers: SOC2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration, and cost vs latency tradeoffs on burst traffic. Next steps are pricing, security docs, and a benchmark run with their sample traffic.

Topics detected:
- Current utilization and headroom (prefix caching behavior)
- Region activation (eu-west-2, ap-southeast-1) and egress concerns
- Private deployment / VPC + KMS requirements for PII model scoring
- Pricing buckets and contract amendment duration
- Performance benchmark plan and success criteria

Action items (captured during call):
- Lena: updated pricing worksheet and contract amendment draft (due 2027-04-23)
- Derek: run KV-cache/latency sensitivity tests and capture p95 and p99 (due 2027-04-25)
- Priya: provide anonymized traffic traces and sequence-length distribution (due 2027-04-22)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: ok everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, quick rollcall?
[00:04] Priya Menon: yeah hey Priya here, Markus and Jolie on the line too.
[00:06] Markus Voss: Markus here, hi.
[00:08] Jolie Kim: Jolie.
[00:10] Derek Shaw: Derek from Redwood, hi all.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: cool, we're here for the renewal check-in and to talk about the planned capacity bump and region add, should be 30-ish minutes with Q&A, we'll take notes.
[00:20] Priya Menon: to set context, our current commit was covering US + cache nodes; last quarter we hit a sustained 18% growth and relative peaks during our nightly ingest, so leadership wants to plan for a 25% reserved uplift and add eu-west and ap-southeast for latency. also some of our clinical customers demand data residency so we need a private path for those models.
[00:37] Lena Ortiz: got it. when you say private path, are you thinking full Private deployment or VPC-hosted Redwood Dedicated?
[00:44] Priya Menon: likely Private for PII models, but we could do Dedicated VPC for less sensitive scoring. main question is integrations — we use AWS KMS and need HSM-backed keys for a subset.
[00:53] Derek Shaw: we support KMS integrations and can point to our HSM guidance; note that Private deployments have a different lead time — typically 6-8 weeks for onprem or VPC with your networking team. for Dedicated VPC that's faster but still needs peering and firewall rules.
[01:10] Markus Voss: latency is critical for eu users. what's your expected 95th percentile latency in eu-west for the Llama-ish models we run? our average seq len is around 700 tokens for summarization.
[01:20] Derek Shaw: for a quantized M-pref model with KV caching, p95 is usually in the 180-250ms range in a colocated eu cluster; but it depends on batch behavior and how much prefix caching you get. with longer sequences latency bumps — we can simulate with your trace.
[01:34] Jolie Kim: by "prefix caching" you mean the automatic KV cache that Redwood keeps for similar prompt prefixes?
[01:38] Derek Shaw: yeah, exactly, prefix and KV caching. in our telemetry heavy prefix reuse can drop per-token cost and tail latency, but if you have very diverse prompts then caching helps less.
[01:50] Priya Menon: our prompts vary a lot in the first 3 turns but then standardized templates after that, so we expect middling cache hit rates. we'll share traces.
[01:58] Evan Reed: quick procurement question — our legal team asked about contract extension length. Do we get a discount for a 12 vs 24 month commit?
[02:06] Lena Ortiz: yes, we have tiered economics; Derek can show the worksheet. 24 months gives steeper discounts and committed burst pools are cheaper per-RU. I'll send the worksheet; we'll run three scenarios: 12-month moderate uplift, 24-month stretch, and a 12-month with optional 6-month extension.
[02:21] Derek Shaw: operational note — when you add eu and ap regions we recommend staged activation: start with eu-west-2 with small pool, run traffic for two weeks, tune batchers and cache TTLs, then open ap-southeast. regional failover policies also important, do you want automatic fallback to US or strict region-only?
[02:38] Priya Menon: for GDPR workloads, region-only. for non-sensitive scoring, fallback to US is ok.
[02:44] Derek Shaw: perfect — we can model routing policies by route. also note egress pricing if you pull model outputs out of region; we'll document that in the pricing worksheet.
[02:54] Markus Voss: about Private deployment — what's the typical audit surface we need to cover? SOC2 is table stakes but we also need access logs and immutable audit trails for certain customers.
[03:03] Aisha Rahman: hi this is Aisha, our CSM — we can provide our SOC2 report and advise on audit log configuration. for Private we add additional audit hooks and you can ship logs to your SIEM via encrypted forwarder.
[03:12] Priya Menon: great. can you confirm support for SAML SSO and RBAC at route level?
[03:17] Aisha Rahman: yes SAML/SSO is supported in the control plane and RBAC can be applied per-project or per-route depending on your tenancy model. we'll include sample policies.
[03:26] Jolie Kim: operational challenge — our SRE worried about warmup costs when we spin new regional pools in high-traffic times; curious whether Redwood has burst pool options to minimize latency without always paying for idle GPUs.
[03:36] Derek Shaw: we do reserved and burst capacity options; burst uses pre-warmed fractional capacity and autoscaling. there's a small startup delta but it's much lower than cold starts — that's a configuration tradeoff we'll capture in the worksheet.
[03:48] Priya Menon: Markus also wanted to know about model variants — can you automatically fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if the primary model is saturated?
[03:56] Derek Shaw: yep, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants; you can chain by latency/cost tier and have automatic fallback and degrade gracefully.
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: ok let's talk numbers briefly — you mentioned 25% uplift; do you have target RU/day or peak qps we should size against?
[04:12] Priya Menon: rough numbers: current committed is ~50k RU/day, peaks to 90k during campaigns, so we'd like to commit to 70-90k for reserve to be safe.
[04:20] Derek Shaw: good to capture the peak distribution; we'll size both sustained reserve and burst headroom. also will include recommended quantization profile for your model family.
[04:29] Evan Reed: timeline from procurement side: once we get the pricing worksheet and SOC2, we can internal review within 5 business days; signature target is end of May.
[04:36] Lena Ortiz: sounds reasonable. we'll aim to send the worksheet and security bundle within 48 hours.
[04:40] Priya Menon: one more FYI — a couple of our customers asked about on-premise airgap options for a limited set of models; is that doable?
[04:47] Derek Shaw: yes, we have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments, but that has longer lead time and is typically a separate commercial path. we'll flag that as an option and outline requirements.
[04:56] Markus Voss: any concerns about tokenization differences or consistent embedding space across regions? we do embeddings centrally and want consistent vectors.
[05:04] Derek Shaw: embeddings use the same model weights and tokenizers — the runtime ensures determinism; however numerics can differ slightly across hardware/quantization modes so we'll document reproducibility and can run side-by-side checks.
[05:16] Aisha Rahman: ok we've captured action items, Lena will send pricing, Derek will run the bench, Priya will share traces.
[05:23] Lena Ortiz: quick recap and owners. Lena: pricing + contract amendment (48 hrs), Derek: KV-cache latency runs (by 4/25), Priya: provide traces (by 4/22). schedule benchmark week of 4/26 — we'll propose two options on calendar. anyone else?
[05:36] Priya Menon: that works. thanks everyone.
[05:39] Evan Reed: thanks.
[05:41] Derek Shaw: thanks all, will follow up with pre-benchmark checklist.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: end call.
